Appeal Department  
Ambetter from Magnolia Health  
111 East Capitol Street, Suite 500  
Jackson, MS 39201  

Re: Rowan Jennings  
Member ID: W965543948  
Reference number: POC-AAA1CF805A-66883  
Requested procedure: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at C5-C6  
CPT: 22551  
Date of denial notice: August 14, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, CPT 22551. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The imaging and clinical records do support this procedure because they demonstrate a specific structural lesion, nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic symptoms, objective weakness, and failure of extensive conservative treatment.

The June 7, 2026 cervical MRI documents a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root. These are not nonspecific or incidental findings. They identify the affected level and provide an anatomic explanation for the patient’s symptoms.

The patient has progressive right-sided radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness. The examination also documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the C5-C6 imaging abnormality and C6 nerve-root distribution. Thus, the imaging findings correlate with both the patient’s symptoms and the examination findings.

The patient has also completed substantial nonoperative treatment without adequate improvement:

- Twelve months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- Eight months of NSAID treatment with inadequate relief.
- Ten weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 10, 2026, through June 19, 2026, totaling 16 completed visits.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 23, 2026, which provided only four weeks of partial relief.

The patient continues to have disabling radicular pain, numbness, and weakness despite these measures. Continued conservative treatment has therefore not adequately controlled the condition or resolved the neurologic deficit.

The record also does not identify the principal risk factors that might otherwise complicate surgery. The patient has no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and does not smoke. The requested surgery is being recommended by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, for the documented C5-C6 lesion and corresponding C6 neurologic impairment.

I request that Ambetter overturn the denial and approve CPT 22551. If the denial is not overturned, please provide the complete clinical-review rationale, identify every criterion determined not to be satisfied, identify the exact guideline and version applied, and explain why the MRI findings of severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve-root compression do not support medical necessity when considered together with the corresponding neurologic symptoms, weakness, examination findings, and failed conservative care.

The plan’s governing policy has not been publicly verified, so the plan has not been quoted in this appeal. Please provide the specific medical-necessity criteria applied to this request so that the patient and treating surgeon can address any remaining issue.

Please include the enclosed clinical records in the appeal review:

- June 7, 2026 cervical MRI report.
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from April 10 through June 19, 2026.
- Medication and treatment history documenting eight months of NSAID use and the April 23, 2026 corticosteroid injection.
- Orthopedic examination and clinical assessment by Duval, MD.
- Prior authorization denial notice dated August 14, 2026.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and issue a written determination. This appeal must be received by February 10, 2027.

Sincerely,

Rowan Jennings
